newsitem.title: USA: Cheesecake Factory sees lower Q4 net.
newsitem.headline: Cheesecake Factory sees lower Q4 net.

text.p: The Cheesecake Factory Inc said it expects to take certain charges in the fourth quarter that will cause its net income to be "significantly below" the $0.19 per share earned in the year-ago quarter.

It also said it expects to report fourth quarter sales of $36.9 million, up about 29 percent from the year-ago fourth quarter. It said it expects comparable restaurant sales to be up about five percent.
The mean estimate for the fourth quarter is for earnings per share of $0.17, according to First Call.

It said unusual charges in the quarter totaled about $0.12 per share and were due to the liquidation of certain debt securities as well as the writeoff of a receivable related to its investment portfolio. It said charges related to the settlement of an employment practices claim and the disposition of certain bakery inventor items that did not meet quality standards.
"By resolving these issues during fiscal 1996, we are able to enter fiscal 1997 with expectations for improving performance," Chairman and Chief Executive Oficer David Overton, said in a statement.
During 1997, he said, the comany aimed to increase productive square footage and restaurant operating weeks by 25 to 30 percent.
